os-web-api.title: API host
os-web-api.summary: The common base of an ASP.NET Core API: validated settings, one answer shape for every result, JWT tokens, central error handling, request language, versioned routes with OpenAPI and Scalar, CORS, rate limiting, background jobs and a secret key ring.

gives.1: Two calls, `AddOSWebApi` and `UseOSWebApi`, set up the whole API pipeline from one configuration section that is checked at startup.
gives.2: Every answer has the same shape (`OSResult`), and an unhandled error becomes a safe 500 with a trace id while the details go to the error sink.
gives.3: The parts an API usually needs are ready: JWT, versioned routes, docs, CORS, rate limit, long-running jobs with progress, and keys for secrets.

sample.quick: A working API host in a few lines
sample.secured: The same host with a key ring for secrets

start.title: Getting started
start.summary: Register the host, add the middleware, and see what the pipeline does.

1.title: One registration
1.text: `AddOSWebApi` registers the API host from your configuration.

2.title: Fixed order
2.text: `UseOSWebApi` adds the middleware in a fixed order.

3.title: Fail at startup
3.text: A wrong value throws an `OSException` at startup.

4.title: Secret keys
4.text: `AddOSSecretKeys` keeps the keys of `ISecretBox` in a folder.

1.title: Registering the host
1.text:
`AddOSWebApi` reads the configuration section `os-api` into `WebApiOptions` and checks it. Then it registers controllers, versioning, OpenAPI, authentication, the error handler, CORS and the rate limiter according to those options.

A wrong value throws an `OSException` at startup, so a broken configuration never reaches a request. There is no callback to change options in code: apps and tests override values through configuration.

2.title: Middleware order
2.text:
`UseOSWebApi` adds the middleware in a fixed order: forwarded headers, the error handler, HSTS (outside Development), HTTPS redirection, static files, request localization, CORS, rate limit, authentication, authorization and the controllers.

The docs endpoints are added when they are enabled.

3.title: Request language
3.text:
The request language needs the registry of `OS.Locale`, so call `AddOSLocale` once before.

The language is taken from the query string first. The names `culture`, `cult` and `lang` work, and short names such as `en` work too. Then it uses the usual headers, and falls back to the configured or default culture.

4.title: Secret keys
4.text:
For secrets, `AddOSSecretKeys` keeps the keys of `ISecretBox` in a folder. They are encrypted with a certificate or, on Windows, with DPAPI.

On other systems it logs a warning that the files are not encrypted. So restrict the folder to the app's identity.

register.title: Register and run
register.note: `AddOSWebApi` also returns the options it read, in case the app needs a value.

first-request.title: The first request
first-request.note: A controller answers on the versioned route and the answer has the common shape.

language.title: The request language
language.note: The default is the first registered culture; `?lang=en` switches the answer to English.

key-ring.title: The key ring on disk
key-ring.note: A key is created on first use and read again later; the file holds only protected bytes. This sample uses a throwaway provider; the real one comes from `AddOSSecretKeys`.

type.WebApiEx: Registration and middleware for the API host.
type.SecretKeysEx: Registers the key ring that `ISecretBox` uses.
type.SecretKeysOptions: How the key files are protected: certificate or DPAPI.
type.DataProtectionKeyRing: A key ring that stores each key in its own protected file.
type.IApiPipelineStep: A step that another package adds to the request pipeline, run after authentication and before authorization; `UseOSWebApi` calls every registered step.

WebApiEx.AddOSWebApi: Reads and checks the `os-api` section and registers the host. Throws `OSException` for a wrong value.
WebApiEx.UseOSWebApi: Adds the middleware in the documented order and maps the controllers.
WebApiEx.UseOSWebApiDocs: Adds the OpenAPI and Scalar endpoints even outside Development; calling it twice is harmless.
WebApiEx.AddOSJob: Registers a background job and the runner that executes it.

SecretKeysEx.AddOSSecretKeys: Stores secret keys in the given folder and registers `ISecretBox` on top of them.

options.title: Settings
options.summary: Every key of the `os-api` section, its default, and what is refused at startup.

1.title: One section
1.text: All settings live in the `os-api` section and are validated together.

3.title: Safe defaults
3.text: `rate-limit` is off, and the docs exist only in Development.

4.title: Secret key
4.text: Keep `jwt:key` in user secrets or the environment, never in the repository.

1.title: Reading the settings
1.text:
All settings live in one section, `os-api`, and are read with `ReadOSConfig`. So they are validated together before the app starts.

`app-code` is required. Keys use kebab-case in configuration files. The rest of the list is `max-upload-bytes`, `static-files`, `forwarded-headers` and `hsts`.

2.title: CORS origins
2.text:
`origins` lists the sites allowed by CORS. Each one must be an absolute http or https origin without a path.

A trailing slash is ignored.

3.title: JWT
3.text:
`jwt` turns on token authentication. When it is enabled, the key must be at least 32 bytes, and the issuer and audience are required.

`previous-keys` keep old tokens valid while a key is rotated. The secret `jwt:key` belongs in user secrets or the environment, never in the repository.

4.title: Versions and docs
4.text:
`api-version` sets the default version, the list of versions and the route prefix. `rate-limit` is off by default.

`docs` is empty by default, which means the docs endpoints exist only in Development. Set it to true or false to decide explicitly.

defaults.title: The defaults
defaults.note: JWT and rate limit are off, the version is 1.0 and docs follow the environment.

from-configuration.title: Read from configuration
from-configuration.note: The origin loses its trailing slash; any key you do not set keeps its default.

bad-origin.title: An origin with a path
bad-origin.note: Rejected at startup, before the first request.

short-key.title: A JWT key that is too short
short-key.note: A short key would be easy to guess, so the app refuses to start.

bad-version.title: A version that is not a number

type.RateLimitOptions: A fixed window per user or IP.
type.WebApiCodes: Names the package uses: section, policy and the error codes it returns.

controllers.title: Controllers and answers
controllers.summary: Base controllers that answer with one shape, and helpers for claims and uploads.

1.title: Base controller
1.text: Derive from `ApiController` and return its helpers.

2.title: One answer shape
2.text: The HTTP status comes from the result and the body is always the same.

1.title: Helpers and answer shape
1.text:
Derive from `ApiController` and return the helpers it offers: `ApiOk`, `ApiNotFound` and `ApiInvalid`. `ApiResult` works for any `OSResult`.

The HTTP status comes from the result's status and the body is always the same. It holds `succeeded`, `status`, `code`, `message`, `traceId`, `errors` and `data`, with the trace id filled in for you.

2.title: Routes
2.text:
Routes are lowercase and sit under `api/v{version}`. So `OrdersController` answers on `/api/v1/orders`.

`ApiAuthorizedController` is the same controller with `[Authorize]`.

3.title: User and files
3.text:
Inside a controller, `GetUserId`, `GetUsername` and `IsAuthenticated` read the signed-in user.

`HttpEx` adds the same to `ClaimsPrincipal` for other code. It also has a way to read the trace id of a request.

`ToBytesAsync` is for an uploaded file with a size limit. When the file is too large, it answers `Invalid` with a clear code instead of reading it.

orders.title: A controller
orders.note: Found, not found and invalid input all use the same answer shape.

reply.title: What the client receives
reply.note: The trace id lets a user report a problem that you can find in the logs.

status-codes.title: Status to HTTP code
status-codes.note: The mapping is fixed, so clients can rely on it.

user-from-token.title: The user of a request
user-from-token.note: The id comes from the `sub` or name identifier claim; a bad value gives none.

upload.title: An upload with a limit
upload.note: The size is checked before the file is read.

type.ApiController: Base of API controllers: versioned route, JSON, answer helpers.
type.ApiAuthorizedController: The same, for signed-in users only.
type.HttpEx: Claims, trace id and uploaded file helpers.

auth.title: Tokens (JWT)
auth.summary: Turn on bearer tokens with configuration and create them with `ITokenService`.

1.title: Token check
1.text: `jwt:enabled` makes every bearer token fully validated.

2.title: Creating tokens
2.text: `ITokenService.Create` signs a token with a unique id.

3.title: Key rotation
3.text: The old key moves to `previous-keys`, and old tokens stay valid until they expire.

4.title: Login is yours
4.text: Login itself is up to the app.

1.title: Checking tokens
1.text:
Set `jwt:enabled` and the pipeline validates the issuer, the audience, the signature and the lifetime of every bearer token, with two minutes of clock tolerance.

The docs get a Bearer scheme and the protected operations are marked.

2.title: Creating a token
2.text:
`ITokenService.Create` signs a token with the claims you give. It adds a unique id called `jti` and returns a `TokenModel` with the token, its expiry and the scheme.

The lifetime is `exp-days` unless you pass one.

When JWT is disabled, it answers `Unavailable` with the code `web.jwt_disabled`. A missing key answers `web.jwt_key_missing`. Nothing throws.

3.title: Key rotation and login
3.text:
To rotate the signing key, put the new key in `key` and move the old one to `previous-keys`. New tokens use the new key and old tokens stay valid until they expire.

Login itself, meaning how you find the user, is up to the app (or the Identity package).

configure.title: Configuration
configure.note: The key comes from user secrets or the environment, not from code.

login.title: A login endpoint
login.note: The token model is the `data` of the answer.

create.title: Create a token
create.note: The expiry is counted from the clock in `TimeProvider`, which a test can replace.

disabled.title: JWT disabled
disabled.note: A normal answer instead of an exception.

short-lifetime.title: A short lifetime
short-lifetime.note: For a one-time link, ask for minutes instead of days.

type.TokenModel: A token, when it expires and its scheme.

errors.title: Handling errors
errors.summary: An unhandled exception becomes a safe 500 and a report, and the client never sees the details.

1.title: Safe 500
1.text: The client gets a 500 with a generic message and the trace id.

3.title: Closed connection
3.text: If the client closes the connection, nothing is reported.

4.title: Results, not exceptions
4.text: Return an `OSResult` for expected failures, not an exception.

1.title: What the client sees
1.text:
`ApiExceptionHandler` catches every exception that no controller handled.

The client gets a 500 with the common answer shape. The code is `web.unhandled`, with a generic message and the trace id. The message and the stack trace are not in the response.

2.title: Logging and reporting
2.text:
The same exception is logged. When an `IErrorSink` is registered, for example from OS.Diagnostics, it is reported there with the trace id, method, route, status and user. So a report and a user's complaint can be matched.

A failing sink never breaks the answer.

3.title: Closed connection and expected failures
3.text:
If the client closed the connection, the request ends with 499 and nothing is reported, because that is not an error.

Validation problems and expected failures should not be exceptions. Return an `OSResult` from the controller instead.

sink.title: A sink of your own
sink.note: Any class that takes an `ErrorReport` will do; OS.Diagnostics provides a ready one.

register.title: Register the sink
register.note: The handler picks it up on its own.

reply.title: What the client sees
reply.note: A code and a trace id, and no detail about the cause.

report.title: What the sink gets
report.note: The full report stays on the server side.

type.ApiExceptionHandler: The central handler for unhandled exceptions.

docs.title: Docs and versions
docs.summary: OpenAPI documents per version, the Scalar page, and how versions are written.

1.title: Document per version
1.text: A separate OpenAPI document is published for each version.

2.title: Scalar page
2.text: The Scalar page is at `/scalar`, with a redirect from `/`.

3.title: Development only
3.text: By default the docs exist only in Development.

4.title: Bearer mark
4.text: Protected operations are marked with the Bearer scheme.

1.title: Documents and Scalar
1.text:
Routes live under `api/v{version}`, and the version is read from the URL.

A document is published for each version in `api-version:items`, at `/openapi/v1.json`, `/openapi/v2.json` and so on. The Scalar page is at `/scalar`, with a redirect to it from `/`.

2.title: Opening and closing the docs
2.text:
By default the docs exist only in Development.

Set `docs` to true to open them elsewhere or to false to close them. You can also call `UseOSWebApiDocs` yourself.

3.title: What the documents show
3.text:
The documents mark protected operations with the Bearer scheme and show `ResultStatus` as text.

Numeric enums such as `JobState` are shown as numbers with their names, which is exactly how they are sent. `ApiVersionText` reads version texts such as `1`, `1.0` and `2.1` and builds the document names.

document-names.title: One document per version
document-names.note: A version without a minor number has a short name; the default version comes first.

versions.title: Reading version texts
versions.note: Anything that is not a number is refused.

off-by-default.title: Closed outside Development
off-by-default.note: The endpoint does not exist unless you turn the docs on.

enums.title: Enums as they are sent
enums.note: The schema matches the real JSON, so generated clients agree with the server.

type.ApiVersionText: Parses versions such as `2.1` and names their documents.

jobs.title: Background jobs
jobs.summary: Start a long task, watch its progress, cancel it, and keep its failures private.

1.title: Job class
1.text: A job is a class that implements `IApiJob`.

2.title: Four endpoints
2.text: `ApiJobController` gives preview, start, progress and cancel.

3.title: One run at a time
3.text: Only one run of each kind is allowed at a time.

4.title: Closed by default
4.text: A job with a permission runs only when a gate allows it.

1.title: Writing a job
1.text:
A job is a class that implements `IApiJob`. It has a `Kind`, the phases it goes through, a plan and the work itself. The plan shows what it would do without changing anything.

Register it with `AddOSJob` and add a controller that derives from `ApiJobController`. It then offers a preview on `GET {kind}/plan`, start on `POST {kind}`, progress on `GET {kind}` and cancel on `DELETE {kind}`. All of them are for signed-in users.

2.title: Running
2.text:
`JobRunner` allows one run of a kind at a time. A second start while it runs answers `Conflict` with the current status.

While it runs, the job reports phases, counts and a note through `JobProgress`, and the status includes the elapsed and remaining time.

Cancelling, or stopping the app, ends the run through its cancellation token.

3.title: Failures and permission
3.text:
If the job throws, the client only sees the code `web.job_failed`. The exception is logged and reported to the error sink.

A job with a `Perm` runs only when an `IJobGate` allows it. With no gate registered the answer is `Forbidden`, which fails closed.

`JobState` is sent as a number, so clients such as OS.Blazor read it directly.

job.title: A job
job.note: Two phases; the loop reports progress and respects cancellation.

controller.title: The controller
controller.note: Nothing to write: the base class has the four endpoints.

gate.title: Who may run it
gate.note: Your own rule; the package does not know about roles or permissions.

register.title: Register
register.note: The job, the gate and the accessor the gate uses.

run.title: Run a job
run.note: The result is kept in the status after the run ends.

failure.title: A job that fails
failure.note: The client sees only the code; the message with the cause stays on the server.

type.ApiJobController: Plan, start, status and cancel endpoints for registered jobs.
type.IApiJob: A background job: kind, phases, plan and run.
type.IJobGate: Decides whether the caller may use a job that needs a permission.
type.JobProgress: How a job reports phases, counts and notes.
type.JobRunner: Runs one job of each kind at a time.
type.JobStatus: A snapshot of a run: state, progress, times and result.
type.JobState: Idle, running, done, failed or cancelled, sent as a number.
